322	  query parameter other than `field` (a missing, blank or repeated `field` is
323	  likewise a `422`); unknown dataset/version/field → `404`, with `404`
324	  taking precedence over every `422` except that a repeated `field` is judged
325	  before the field lookup and is therefore always a `422`.
326	
327	  Impact results are cached persistently (they survive restarts) and every
328	  read reflects the currently committed lineage graph: creating a schema
329	  version invalidates the cache entries related to that dataset, and creating
330	  or deleting a lineage mapping invalidates the cached impacts of the
331	  mapping's source field and of every field that can reach it. Unrelated
332	  cache entries are preserved.
333	
334	### Quality rules
335	
336	Quality rules validate rows against a schema version. Rules are version-scoped
337	and persisted (including their enabled state) across restarts.
338	
339	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — create a rule.
340	  Body: `{"name": "id required", "kind": "not_null", "params": {...}}`. Returns
341	  `201` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `params`, `enabled`, `created_at`; `enabled`
342	  defaults to `true`. Rule names must be unique within a version (`409` on
343	  conflict). Referenced dataset/version/field must exist (`404`); other invalid
344	  input returns `422` and nothing is written. Supported kinds:
345	  - `not_null` — params `{"field": "<existing field>"}`.
346	  - `numeric_range` — params `{"field": "<existing field>", "min": <finite
347	    number>, "max": <finite number>}` with `min <= max`.
348	  - `unique` — params `{"fields": ["<existing field>", ...]}`: a non-empty list
349	    of distinct, existing field names.
350	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules` — list rules
351	  sorted by `id` ascending.
352	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/{rule_id}` —
353	  enable or disable a rule. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
354	  the updated rule. Unknown rule/dataset/version → `404`.
355	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluate` —
356	  evaluate rows. Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}`. Only enabled rules run.
357	  Returns `{"dataset", "version", "results"}` with results sorted by `rule_id`;
358	  each result has `rule_id`, `name`, `passed` and `violations` (0-based row
359	  indices in ascending order).
360	  - `not_null` fails on missing or `null` values.
361	  - `numeric_range` fails on missing, `null`, non-numeric, boolean or
362	    out-of-range values (boundaries included).
363	  - `unique` compares the tuple of `fields` values per row; a missing field
364	    counts as `null`, and every row taking part in a duplicate group is a
365	    violation.
366	  - With an empty `rows` list every rule passes.
367	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations` —
368	  list the persisted evaluation history of the version, ordered by `sequence`
369	  (occurrence order). Every successful evaluation appends one immutable
370	  summary (`sequence`, `dataset`, `version`, `row_count`,
371	  `violation_row_count` — the number of distinct submitted rows violating at
372	  least one rule — `results` and `created_at`); rejected or failed
373	  evaluations leave no record, and an empty `rows` submission is recorded
374	  with zero violations. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
375	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
376	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/evaluations/diff`
377	  — read-only diff between the two most recent recorded evaluations
378	  (`from_sequence` → `to_sequence`). `added_violation_rows` /
379	  `removed_violation_rows` are the 0-based row indices that started or
380	  stopped violating any rule, and each entry of `rules` carries the rule's
381	  `before`/`after` side (`violation_count` and `violations`), the per-rule
382	  `added_violations` / `removed_violations` and the numeric
383	  `violation_count_delta` (negative, zero or positive). A rule missing from
384	  one side (disabled or created between the two evaluations) has a `null`
385	  side and `null` row-level diff fields. With fewer than two recorded
386	  evaluations the response is an explicit empty result (null sequences,
387	  empty lists), not an error. Same `404`/`422` rules as the history
388	  endpoint; nothing is written.
389	
390	### Quality anomaly detection
391	
392	Anomaly detection runs over the persisted evaluation history of a schema
393	version. A version carries at most one detection config; scans append
394	immutable anomaly records that persist across restarts.
395	
396	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
397	  — register the version's detection config. The body contains exactly three
398	  integers: `consecutive_worsening_steps` (at least `2`),
399	  `violation_row_limit` and `rule_violation_limit` (both non-negative).
400	  Returns `201` with the config (`id`, `dataset`, `version`, the three
401	  thresholds, `created_at`). A second config for the same version returns
402	  `409`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing, extra, non-integer or
403	  out-of-range fields → `422` and nothing is written.
404	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection`
405	  — return the registered config (`404` when none exists). The endpoint takes
406	  no request body and no query parameters (`422`).
407	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/scan`
408	  — run one detection pass over the persisted evaluation history and return
409	  the anomaly records this scan newly added (ordered by `id`); they are
410	  persisted in the same transaction. Scanning without a registered config
411	  returns `409`; an empty history is a successful scan that writes nothing.
412	  The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`). Each
413	  record has `id`, `kind`, `sequence` (the history sequence it points to),
414	  `rule_id`, `violation_count` and `created_at`; `kind` is one of:
415	  - `row_limit` — the evaluation's `violation_row_count` exceeds
416	    `violation_row_limit` (`rule_id` is `null`).
417	  - `rule_limit` — one rule's violation count in the evaluation exceeds
418	    `rule_violation_limit`; `rule_id` carries the rule's id.
419	  - `trend` — the violation row counts of adjacent evaluations strictly
420	    increase and the consecutive increase count at the tail of the history
421	    reaches `consecutive_worsening_steps`; the record points to the final
422	    evaluation of the increasing sequence (`rule_id` is `null`). A shorter
423	    run or any decline produces no trend record.
424	
425	  A record with the same kind, history sequence and rule id is never
426	  duplicated: repeated scans only persist and return newly appearing
427	  anomalies, and concurrent scans store each anomaly exactly once with
428	  contiguous ids.
429	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/anomaly-detection/anomalies`
430	  — list every anomaly record of the version sorted by `id` ascending (empty
431	  when there are none, never an error). Same `404`/`422` rules as the scan
432	  endpoint; nothing is written.
433	
434	### Quality gate
435	
436	The quality gate is the release-readiness verdict of a schema version. It is
437	computed fresh from the persisted records on every read — nothing is cached,
438	re-run or written, and the rule definitions are never consulted (violations
439	recorded for rules since disabled still count).
440	
441	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate` — return the
442	  verdict as a deterministic JSON document (fixed key order, compact
443	  whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
444	  `{"dataset", "version", "verdict", "reasons", "counts"}`.
445	  - `verdict` is one of:
446	    - `pass` — the latest recorded evaluation passed every rule and no
447	      anomaly record exists; a zero-violation evaluation left by an empty
448	      `rows` submission is a valid basis.
449	    - `undetermined` — no evaluation was ever recorded; `reasons` is empty
450	      and the read succeeds (never an error).
451	    - `fail` — the latest recorded evaluation still has violating rows, or
452	      the version carries any anomaly record.
453	  - `reasons` lists every factor that lowers the verdict, sorted by `kind`,
454	    `sequence` and `rule_id` (null ids first), all ascending. Each reason has
455	    `kind`, `sequence`, `rule_id` and `violation_count` (a missing rule id is
456	    `null`, never omitted). Every rule with violations in the latest
457	    evaluation contributes one `violation` reason with its violation row
458	    count; every persisted anomaly record contributes one reason of its own
459	    kind (`row_limit`, `rule_limit` or `trend`). A rule that appears in both
460	    yields two reasons — they are never merged or deduplicated.
461	  - `counts` reports how many persisted records the verdict examined:
462	    `evaluations`, `anomalies` and `reasons` (the length of the reason list).
463	  - The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters: any body
464	    bytes — including whitespace-only ones — or any query parameter are a
465	    `422`, checked after the path dataset/version resolves (`404` first).
466	    Nothing is written on any rejection.
467	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/quality-rules/gate/at?timestamp=...`
468	  — the same verdict as it stood at a requested instant. `timestamp` must be
469	  a timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time; only evaluations and anomaly records
470	  written at or before it count, and the latest evaluation of that window is
471	  the one with the highest sequence inside it. The response is the same
472	  deterministic document as the bare gate (`dataset`, `version`, `verdict`,
473	  `reasons`, `counts`, one trailing newline), with the counts covering only
474	  the records inside the window. A window without any evaluation is
475	  `undetermined` with an empty reason list — a normal response, never an
476	  error. The endpoint accepts GET only and is strictly read-only. The path
477	  dataset/version resolves first (`404`); afterwards any request body bytes
478	  (whitespace-only included), a missing, repeated, unparseable or
479	  timezone-less `timestamp`, or any other query parameter are a `422` that
480	  writes nothing.
481	
482	### Privacy policies
483	
484	Privacy policies attach a sensitivity classification and masking strategy to a
485	single field of a schema version, enabling role-based de-identification of row
486	data. Policies (including their enabled state) are persisted across restarts.
487	
488	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — register a
489	  policy. Body:
490	  `{"field": "email", "classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles": ["analyst"]}`.
491	  `field` must name an existing field of the version; `classification` is a
492	  non-empty string; `masking` is `redact` or `partial`; `allowed_roles` is an
493	  array of distinct, non-empty role names and may be empty. Returns `201` with
494	  the submitted fields plus `id`, `enabled` (defaults to `true`) and
495	  `created_at`. Registering two policies for the same field within one version
496	  returns `409`. Unknown dataset/version/field → `404`; other invalid input →
497	  `422` and nothing is written.
498	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies` — list policies
499	  sorted by `id` ascending.
500	- `PATCH /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
501	  enable or disable a policy. Body: `{"enabled": true}` (boolean only); returns
502	  the updated policy. Unknown policy/dataset/version → `404`.
503	- `PUT /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/{policy_id}` —
504	  revise a policy. Body carries exactly the three adjustable fields:
505	  `{"classification": "PII", "masking": "partial", "allowed_roles":
506	  ["analyst"]}`, using the same value rules as registration — a non-empty
507	  `classification` after trimming, `masking` of `redact` or `partial`, and an
508	  `allowed_roles` array of distinct, non-empty-after-trimming role names that
509	  may be empty. The three fields are replaced together from one whole
510	  submission. The revision never changes the policy id, the field it belongs
511	  to, its `enabled` state or its `created_at`; it writes only the policy
512	  itself — no policy is created, no identification record is touched and no
513	  masking suggestion is registered. Returns `200` with the updated policy in
514	  the same shape as the policy read, and the revision survives restarts. The
515	  next privacy view read (and every later masked read) judges each value by
516	  the revised classification, masking and allowed roles. Already-written
517	  masking-hit records, access records and cleanup requests are unaffected —
518	  their contents and ordering stay as written; the grouping of the summary,
519	  diff and reconciliation responses keeps the same counting rules, while the
520	  policy classification and masking reported on trend rows (and the policy
521	  entries of the coverage check and compliance export) reflect the current
522	  values. Advisory masking suggestions are unaffected. Unknown
523	  dataset/version/policy → `404`, judged before every request-shape check;
524	  missing or extra fields, a blank `classification`, an illegal `masking`
525	  value, duplicate or blank `allowed_roles` entries, an empty or
526	  whitespace-only body, malformed JSON, a non-object payload or any query
527	  parameter → `422` and nothing is written. Concurrent revisions of the same
528	  policy have exactly one winner; the loser receives `409` and changes no
529	  field.
530	
531	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view` — return a
532	  role-scoped, order-preserving copy of submitted rows. Body:
533	  `{"role": "guest", "rows": [{...}, ...]}` with a non-empty `role` and a list
534	  of row objects. Response: `{"dataset", "version", "rows"}`. Only enabled
535	  policies whose field appears in a row mask the value when `role` is not in
536	  `allowed_roles`:
537	  - `redact` replaces every non-`null` value with `"***"`.
538	  - `partial` keeps the first character and last two characters of strings
539	    longer than 4 characters (e.g. `"alice@example.com"` → `"aom"`); every other
540	    non-`null` value (short strings, numbers, booleans, …) is replaced with
541	    `"***"`.
542	  - `null` values and fields without a policy are returned unchanged; rows
543	    missing a covered field are left without it.
544	
545	  Every successful view also appends one audit record per value it actually
546	  masked (the same field masked in several rows yields one record per masked
547	  value; a role in `allowed_roles`, a `null` value, an uncovered field or a
548	  disabled policy never hits); the records are persisted per version and are
549	  append-only.
550	
551	  Every successful view additionally appends exactly one access record,
552	  whether or not it masked any value (an empty `rows` submission is recorded
553	  too). Rejected or failed views leave neither kind of record.
554	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/access-records`
555	  — list every access record of the version, ordered by `sequence` ascending
556	  (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has `sequence`,
557	  `role`, `row_count` (the number of submitted rows), `masked_count` (the
558	  number of masking-hit records the same view wrote, so the two logs
559	  cross-check) and `created_at`. The endpoint takes no request body and no
560	  query parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is
561	  written.
562	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records`
563	  — list every masking-hit record of the version, ordered by `sequence`
564	  ascending (empty when there are none, never an error). Each record has
565	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`. The
566	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
567	  dataset/version → `404`. Nothing is written.
568	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/search`
569	  — read-only filtered retrieval of the same masking-hit records. The
570	  response is the same record collection as the full list (each record has
571	  `sequence`, `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking` and `created_at`),
572	  sorted by `sequence` ascending; a filter that matches nothing returns an
573	  empty array, never an error. All filters are optional query parameters and
574	  combine with AND:
575	  - `role` — exact match against the requesting role recorded on the hit,
576	    case-insensitive (no substring or other fuzzy matching).
577	  - `field` — exact match against the hit field name, case-insensitive.
578	  - `start` / `end` — closed write-time interval: a record matches when its
579	    `created_at` is between the bounds inclusive. Each bound is a
580	    timezone-bearing ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`); either bound may be
581	    given alone. `start` later than `end` → `422`.
582	
583	  The endpoint takes no request body; an unparseable or timezone-less
584	  `start`/`end`, or any query parameter other than `role`, `field`, `start`
585	  and `end`, → `422`. Unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
586	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list. It is strictly read-only:
587	  no record is written, modified or deleted and the summary/diff responses
588	  are unaffected.
589	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/summary`
590	  — read-only compliance summary computed fresh from the persisted records on
591	  every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted). Response:
592	  `{"dataset", "version", "groups"}`; `groups` is an empty array when the
593	  version has no records. Each group merges records with the same `field`,
594	  `policy_id`, `role` and `masking` (different roles or masking modes stay
595	  separate) and lists `field`, `policy_id`, `role`, `masking`, `hit_count`
596	  (one record counts as one hit), `first_hit_at` and `last_hit_at` (the
597	  earliest and latest record `created_at` in the group). Groups sort by
598	  `field`, then `policy_id`, `role` and `masking`, all ascending. The
599	  endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`); unknown
600	  dataset/version → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
601	  record list.
602	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/trend`
603	  — read-only hit trend aggregated by privacy policy, computed fresh from the
604	  persisted records on every read (no caching, nothing is written or deleted).
605	  Hits of the same policy merge across roles (a disabled policy's historical
606	  hits still count). Response: `{"dataset", "version", "policies", "totals"}`;
607	  `policies` is an empty array when the version has no records. Each policy
608	  row carries `policy_id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `total_hits`
609	  and `days`; policies sort by `policy_id` ascending. `days` lists only UTC
610	  calendar days with hits (a write time with a non-zero offset buckets by its
611	  UTC day), sorted ascending with no zero-filled gaps; each entry has `day`
612	  (`YYYY-MM-DD`), `hit_count` (one record counts once), `hit_count_delta`
613	  (difference from the previous listed day, `null` on the first) and `trend`
614	  (`up`/`down`/`flat`, or `none` on the first day). `totals` gives
615	  `total_hits` (the sum of the row totals), `policy_count` (policies with
616	  hits) and `day_count` (distinct hit days over the whole version, the
617	  per-policy day union). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
618	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`, with the same
619	  404-before-422 precedence as the record list.
620	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests`
621	  — open a two-stage retention cleanup request for the version's masking-hit
622	  records. Body contains exactly `reason` and `before`:
623	  `{"reason": "legal hold expired", "before": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`.
624	  `reason` must be a string that is non-empty after trimming whitespace;
625	  `before` must be an ISO-8601 date-time carrying a timezone (offset or `Z`),
626	  and a record belongs to the target set only when its hit write time is
627	  strictly earlier than that instant. Creating a request only returns a
628	  preview — no hit record is deleted or modified, and the record list,
629	  search, summary, diff, reconcile and trend responses stay unchanged.
630	  Returns `201` with `id`, `reason` (trimmed), `before` (echoed as
631	  submitted), `status` (`pending`), `created_at` and a `preview` block:
632	  `hit_count` (the number of records that would be cleaned up),
633	  `first_hit_at` / `last_hit_at` (the earliest and latest hit times in the
634	  target set, `null` when the set is empty) and `fields` (the distinct field
635	  names involved, sorted ascending; `[]` when empty). The target set is
636	  fixed at creation time: masking-hit records written afterwards never enter
637	  the request even when they precede the cutoff by clock time. At most one
638	  pending request may exist per version; creating another while one is open
639	  returns `409` and writes nothing (confirmed requests never block a new
640	  one). Unknown dataset/version → `404`; missing/non-string/blank `reason`,
641	  missing/unparseable/timezone-less `before`, an extra body field, a
642	  non-JSON/non-object body or any query parameter → `422` and nothing is
643	  written, with 404 taking precedence.
644	- `GET .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests` — list the
645	  version's cleanup requests sorted by request `id` ascending (empty when
646	  there are none). Confirmed requests stay listed and requests survive
647	  process restarts. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
648	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
649	- `POST .../privacy-policies/view/audit-records/cleanup-requests/{request_id}/confirm`
650	  — confirm a request with an empty request body and no query parameters.
651	  Confirmation atomically deletes exactly the target set frozen at creation
652	  and sets `status` to `confirmed`; the response is the request plus
653	  `confirmed_at` and `deleted_count` (the number of records actually
654	  deleted, possibly zero). Confirming an already-confirmed request returns
655	  `409` and never changes data again; concurrent confirmations have exactly
656	  one winner (the others get `409`) and can never leave the records half
657	  deleted. After a cleanup the surviving hit records keep their original
658	  `sequence` numbers and later hits continue the existing increasing run
659	  without reusing cleaned numbers; the record list and search return only
660	  surviving records, and summary, trend, diff and reconcile recompute from
661	  them. Access records are not cleaned up and the processing-task audit
662	  chain remains immutable. A request body or query parameter on the confirm
663	  endpoint → `422`; unknown dataset/version/request → `404` (precedence
664	  matches the hit-record reads), and confirming a confirmed request →
665	  `409`.
666	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-compliance-export` — read-only
667	  cross-version export of the dataset's whole privacy compliance state,
668	  computed fresh on every read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or
669	  deleted, and no hit record, access record or cleanup request is touched).
670	  The path carries only the dataset name; the request takes no body and no
671	  query parameters (`422`); an unknown dataset → `404`, with the same
672	  404-before-422 precedence as the hit-record reads. A dataset without
673	  schema versions returns `200` with an empty `versions` array and all-zero
674	  totals, never an error. The JSON document is deterministic (fixed key
675	  order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing newline):
676	
677	  ```json
678	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"policies":[...],"hit_count":0,"masked_count":1,"view_count":2,"cleanup_requests":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
679	  ```
680	
681	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
682	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
683	  has exactly `version`, `policies`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
684	  `view_count`, `cleanup_requests` in that order. `policies` lists the
685	  version's registered policies ordered by policy id; each policy has `id`,
686	  `field`, `classification`, `masking`, `allowed_roles` and `enabled`.
687	  `cleanup_requests` lists the version's cleanup requests ordered by request
688	  id (both pending and confirmed are retained); each has `id`, `reason`,
689	  `status` and `created_at`. `hit_count` is the number of masking-hit
690	  records currently stored for the version, `masked_count` is the sum of the
691	  access records' masked-value counts and `view_count` is the number of
692	  access records; all three reflect the records surviving a confirmed
693	  cleanup. `totals` has exactly `policy_count`, `hit_count`, `masked_count`,
694	  `view_count` and `cleanup_request_count`, each the sum of the per-version
695	  values over the whole dataset.
696	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/privacy-policy-coverage` — read-only cross-version
697	  check of the dataset's privacy policy coverage, computed fresh on every
698	  read (no caching; nothing is written, modified or deleted, and no policy
699	  or identification record is touched). The path carries only the dataset
700	  name; the request takes no body and no query parameters (`422`); an
701	  unknown dataset → `404`, with the same 404-before-422 precedence as the
702	  compliance export. A dataset without schema versions returns `200` with an
703	  empty `versions` array and all-zero totals, never an error. The JSON
704	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly
705	  one trailing newline):
706	
707	  ```json
708	  {"dataset":"orders","versions":[{"version":1,"fields":[...],"candidates":[...]}],"totals":{...}}
709	  ```
710	
711	  The top-level keys are exactly `dataset`, `versions`, `totals` in that
712	  order. `versions` is ordered by version number ascending and each entry
713	  has exactly `version`, `fields`, `candidates` in that order. `fields`
714	  lists every field of the version ordered by field name; each entry has
715	  `field`, `coverage`, `classification`, `masking` and `enabled`, where
716	  `coverage` is `enabled` (an enabled policy is registered), `disabled` (a
717	  policy is registered but disabled) or `unregistered` (no policy), and the
718	  last three keys report the registered policy's classification, masking and
719	  enabled state (all `null` when no policy is registered). `candidates`
720	  lists the advisory suggestions for fields that were identified with at
721	  least one name or sample hit but carry no privacy policy yet, ordered by
722	  identification record id ascending; each candidate has exactly `field`,
723	  `classification` and `masking`, and an identified field whose name and
724	  samples both missed does not appear. The candidates are a compliance
725	  self-check reference only: they never register a policy and never rewrite
726	  an identification record. `totals` has exactly `version_count`,
727	  `field_count`, `enabled_count`, `disabled_count`, `unregistered_count`
728	  and `candidate_count`, each the sum of the per-version values over the
729	  whole dataset.
730	
731	### Sensitive-field identification
732	
733	Sensitive-field identification produces candidate annotations for the fields of
734	a schema version. It complements the manual privacy policies but never creates
735	or modifies one: an identification is advisory only. Records (including their
736	stable ids) persist across restarts.
737	
738	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
739	  identify one field. The body contains exactly `field` and `samples`:
740	  `{"field": "contact_email", "samples": ["alice@example.com"]}`. `field` must
741	  name an existing field of the version; its name and type are taken from the
742	  version definition. `samples` is an array of JSON scalars (strings, numbers,
743	  booleans or `null`) and may be empty; objects or arrays reject the whole
744	  request. The samples are never stored or echoed back. Returns the record;
745	  the first submission for a field returns `201`, re-running the same field
746	  refreshes the record in place (the id is unchanged) and returns `200`.
747	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications` —
748	  return every identification record of the version sorted by id ascending
749	  (empty when there are none). The endpoint takes no request body and no query
750	  parameters (`422`); unknown dataset/version → `404`.
751	
752	  Each record has `id`, `field`, `field_type`, `evidence`, `confidence`,
753	  `source` and `created_at`. `source` references the identified field as
754	  `{"dataset", "version", "field"}`. `evidence` is the ordered, de-duplicated
755	  list of hit kinds, name hits before sample hits:
756	
757	  - **Name hits** — the field name contains a sensitive word case-insensitively
758	    as a substring. The words are `email`, `phone`, `id_card`, `password`,
759	    `token` and `birth`, emitting `name:<word>` in that order.
760	  - **Sample hits** — only string sample values are inspected (numbers,
761	    booleans and `null` never hit), and only when the field's declared type is
762	    `string`; a field declared with any other type is matched by name alone,
763	    even when a sample looks like an email. `sample:email` requires exactly
764	    one `@` with non-empty text on both sides and a dot in the domain;
765	    `sample:phone` requires an 11-digit string starting with `1`. Either format
766	    matching is sufficient.
767	
768	  `confidence` is `high` when both the name and the samples hit, `medium` for
769	  samples only, `low` for the name only and `none` when neither side hits
770	  (`evidence` is then an empty list but the record is still generated).
771	
772	  One record is kept per field: a re-run overwrites the evidence and confidence
773	  in place with a stable id. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; a field that does
774	  not exist in the version → `404`; missing or extra body fields, a
775	  non-string or blank field name, a `samples` value that is not an array of
776	  scalars (objects and arrays included), an empty body, malformed JSON or any
777	  query parameter → `422` and nothing is written.
778	
779	#### Masking strategy suggestions
780	
781	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions`
782	  — read-only advisory masking-strategy candidates derived from the version's
783	  identification records. The endpoint takes no request body and no query
784	  parameters (`422` if either is present, with nothing written); unknown
785	  dataset/version → `404`. A version without identification records returns an
786	  empty list rather than an error.
787	
788	  Each candidate has exactly `field`, `classification`, `masking` and
789	  `allowed_roles`. Only records whose name or samples hit produce a candidate;
790	  a record with empty evidence is omitted. Candidates follow the identification
791	  records' `id` ascending and are recomputed on every read, so refreshing an
792	  identification changes the suggestion on the next request. The endpoint
793	  writes nothing, never registers a privacy policy and leaves the
794	  identification records' fields, ordering and refresh semantics untouched;
795	  the privacy view continues to mask according to registered policies only.
796	
797	  - `classification` is `PII` for email, phone, id-card and birthday hits, and
798	    `CREDENTIAL` for password and token hits. A field hitting both is `PII`.
799	  - `masking` reuses the privacy-view vocabulary: `partial` for `PII`
800	    candidates and `redact` for `CREDENTIAL` candidates (a both-kinds field
801	    takes `partial`); no new masking format is introduced.
802	  - `allowed_roles` is always an empty list: the suggested masking applies to
803	    every role, granting none an unmasked view.
804	
805	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/sensitive-identifications/masking-suggestions/register`
806	  — turn the current advisory candidates into registered privacy policies. The
807	  body contains only `{"fields": ["<field>", ...]}`: a non-empty array of
808	  distinct field names, each non-empty after trimming and naming an existing
809	  field of the version that currently has a masking suggestion candidate.
810	  Returns `201` with one privacy policy record per requested field, in the
811	  request's field-name order; each record has the same fields as the manual
812	  policy creation response (`id`, `field`, `classification`, `masking`,
813	  `allowed_roles`, `enabled`, `created_at`), is enabled by default and gets a
814	  service-generated id and timestamp. Each policy copies its candidate's
815	  `classification` and `masking` verbatim with the candidate's empty
816	  `allowed_roles`, so after registration every role sees those fields masked;
817	  the next privacy view read masks according to the new policies. The whole
818	  batch is validated before anything is written, so any rejection writes no
819	  policy and no timestamp. Unknown dataset/version, or a named field that does
820	  not exist in the version → `404`; a field without an available candidate
821	  (never identified, or whose identification record currently yields no
822	  candidate) or one that already has a privacy policy → `409`; two concurrent
823	  registrations of the same field leave exactly one winner. Missing or extra
824	  body fields, an empty `fields` array, duplicate, non-string or blank names,
825	  an empty body, a whitespace-only body, malformed JSON or any query parameter
826	  → `422` and nothing is written. Registration only reads the identification
827	  records and field definitions; it never writes or auto-refreshes an
828	  identification, and the read-only suggestions endpoint stays unchanged.
829	
830	### Row snapshots
831	
832	A row snapshot persistently records the rows of a schema version at one point in
833	time. Snapshots (including their rows) survive restarts.
834	
835	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — persist a snapshot.
836	  Body: `{"rows": [{...}, ...]}` where `rows` must be an array of JSON objects
837	  (it may be empty). The JSON values and the order of rows/object keys are deep
838	  copied verbatim. A SHA-256 content fingerprint of the saved row sequence is
839	  computed at creation and written together with the rows in one atomic write,
840	  so it can later attest that the persisted rows are unchanged; the fingerprint
841	  is not part of the response, which stays `id`, `dataset`, `version`,
842	  `created_at` and `row_count` (no rows). In the same transaction the service
843	  also maintains the snapshot diff cache incrementally (see "Snapshot diff
844	  cache" below): the canonical form of every row (key-sorted compact JSON text
845	  in stored row order) and the sorted set of top-level field names are written
846	  together with the snapshot, and one `created` record is appended to the
847	  version's cache trail. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; malformed or
848	  non-object rows → `422` and nothing is written.
849	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots` — list snapshot
850	  metadata sorted by `id` ascending (no `rows`).
851	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}` — return
852	  the metadata together with the saved `rows`. Unknown dataset/version/snapshot
853	  → `404`.
854	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/verify` —
855	  read-only content-fingerprint verification, appended one segment after the
856	  single-snapshot read address and accepting GET only. On every read the
857	  fingerprint of the currently persisted row sequence is recomputed and
858	  compared with the fingerprint stored with the snapshot at creation; the
859	  snapshot and its rows are only read, never written or modified. The JSON
860	  document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, lowercase
861	  booleans, exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `dataset`,
862	  `version`, `snapshot_id`, `row_count`, `stored_hash`, `computed_hash` and
863	  `valid` in that order. `stored_hash` is the fingerprint written at creation,
864	  `computed_hash` the freshly recomputed one and `valid` is `true` exactly
865	  while both agree; directly changing, adding, deleting or replacing a saved
866	  row makes them differ and changes `computed_hash`. Both verdicts return
867	  `200`. The fingerprint hashes the saved row sequence as a JSON array in row
868	  order with each object's keys sorted by Unicode code point, compact text,
869	  non-ASCII characters unescaped, UTF-8 encoded and SHA-256 digested to
870	  hexadecimal; array order and value types are significant (integers, floats,
871	  strings and booleans never compare equal and negative zero is represented
872	  distinctly), an empty snapshot is fingerprinted normally and the same rows
873	  yield the same digest across restarts. The verification reads only the
874	  snapshot and its rows — no lineage, quality, privacy or task state — and
875	  does not affect retention or deletion; a confirmed-deleted snapshot is no
876	  longer addressable here either (`404`). The endpoint takes no request body
877	  and no query parameters: any body bytes — including whitespace-only ones —
878	  or any query parameter are a `422`, checked after the path
879	  dataset/version/snapshot resolves, so an unknown dataset, version or
880	  snapshot is a `404` first. Every rejection writes nothing.
881	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at?timestamp=<ISO-8601>` —
882	  return the most recent snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
883	  `timestamp`, including its rows. The timestamp must be a timezone-aware
884	  ISO-8601 date-time (an offset or trailing `Z`): missing, invalid or
885	  timezone-less values return `422`; unknown dataset/version → `404`; when no
886	  snapshot exists at or before the timestamp the response is `404`.
887	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/diff?from=<ISO-8601>&to=<ISO-8601>`
888	  — read-only time-travel row diff, appended one segment after the bare-row
889	  time lookup and accepting GET only. Each of `from` (the baseline) and `to`
890	  (the target) must be a timezone-aware ISO-8601 date-time; each side
891	  independently selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later
892	  than its own timestamp (the same selection as the bare-row lookup), so the
893	  two times may resolve to the same snapshot and a `to` earlier than `from` is
894	  valid — the two snapshots are simply compared in their named order. The
895	  comparison reads snapshots and rows and writes nothing. The JSON document
896	  is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one trailing
897	  newline) with top-level keys `from_timestamp`, `to_timestamp`,
898	  `from_snapshot_id`, `to_snapshot_id`, `added`, `removed`, `fields_added`
899	  and `fields_removed` in that order; the timestamps echo the submitted query
900	  values. `added` and `removed` use the exact comparison semantics of the
901	  snapshot-id diff (JSON-object multisets, key order irrelevant, array order
902	  and value types significant, duplicates counted; entries
903	  `{"row", "count"}` sorted by canonical row text). `fields_added` and
904	  `fields_removed` compare the top-level field names appearing on the
905	  snapshots' row objects: names only on the target side are added, names only
906	  on the baseline side are removed, names on both enter neither set, and each
907	  list sorts by field name ascending. When both times select the same
908	  snapshot all four collections are empty and the request succeeds. Unknown
909	  dataset/version → `404`, checked before every request-shape check; a missing,
910	  blank, repeated, unparseable or timezone-less `from`/`to`, an extra query
911	  parameter or any request body bytes (whitespace-only included) → `422`; a
912	  side with no snapshot at or before its timestamp → `404` and nothing is
913	  written.
914	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/diff/masked` —
915	  role-masked time-travel row diff, appended one segment after the bare-row
916	  time diff and accepting POST only. The body contains exactly `role`,
917	  `from` and `to`: `{"role": "guest", "from": "<ISO-8601>", "to":
918	  "<ISO-8601>"}`; `role` must be non-empty after trimming and each time must
919	  be a timezone-aware ISO-8601 date-time (offset or `Z`). Each side
920	  independently selects the newest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later
921	  than its own timestamp, with exactly the same selection as the bare-row
922	  time lookup. Added and removed entries are first judged and counted from
923	  the raw, unmasked rows with the bare-row diff's JSON-object multiset
924	  semantics (key order irrelevant, array order and value types significant,
925	  duplicates counted): a row appearing several times stays one entry with
926	  its multiplicity, and masking only rewrites the entry's row data — entries
927	  are never merged or split. Entries sort by the canonical (key-sorted) JSON
928	  text of the raw row, so the output order is unaffected by masking. Each
929	  emitted row is then masked exactly as the row-submission privacy view masks
930	  it, applying only the version's currently enabled policies
931	  (`redact`/`partial` semantics, `allowed_roles`, nulls and uncovered fields
932	  behave identically). The response is the same deterministic document as
933	  the bare-row time diff (fixed key order, compact whitespace, exactly one
934	  trailing newline) with the same keys in the same order: `from_timestamp`,
935	  `to_timestamp`, `from_snapshot_id`, `to_snapshot_id`, `added`, `removed`,
936	  `fields_added` and `fields_removed`; the timestamps echo the submitted
937	  body values and the field-name sets carry no values, so masking can never
938	  change them. Every successful read appends one masking-hit record per
939	  value it actually masks, counted per occurrence across both snapshots'
940	  diff entries (an entry of count `n` whose covered value is masked yields
941	  `n` hit records; added-side entries first, then removed-side, each side in
942	  canonical row order), structurally identical to the regular view's hit
943	  records and continuing the same per-version sequence run, plus exactly one
944	  access record whose `row_count` is the total number of rows expanded from
945	  both sides' entries and whose `masked_count` equals the number of hit
946	  records the read wrote. The records enter all existing masking-hit/access
947	  reads, filters, summaries, diffs, reconciliation, trends and cleanup
948	  previews; records of one read share a write timestamp, sequences stay
949	  continuous across processes, and a write obstruction never fails the read.
950	  The read never modifies snapshots, rows, policies or identification
951	  records. Unknown dataset/version → `404`; each side with a usable
952	  timestamp is resolved independently, so a side with no snapshot at or
953	  before its timestamp is likewise `404` and precedes every shape check
954	  (including a missing or invalid timestamp on the other side); a missing or
955	  wrong-typed `role`/`from`/`to`, a role blank after trimming, an
956	  unparseable or timezone-less time, an extra body field, an empty,
957	  whitespace-only or non-JSON body, a non-object body and any query
958	  parameter are `422` and write nothing.
959	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/at/masked-view` —
960	  role-masked time travel, appended one segment after the bare-row time
961	  lookup and accepting POST only. The body contains exactly `role` and
962	  `timestamp`: `{"role": "guest", "timestamp": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`; the
963	  service selects the latest snapshot whose `created_at` is not later than
964	  `timestamp` (the same selection as the bare-row lookup). On success it
965	  returns `{"dataset", "version", "snapshot_id", "created_at", "rows"}`; the
966	  `rows` are an order-preserving copy of the snapshot's rows masked exactly
967	  as the row-submission privacy view masks them, applying only the version's
968	  currently enabled policies (`redact`/`partial` semantics, `allowed_roles`,
969	  nulls and uncovered fields behave identically). Every successful read
970	  appends one masking-hit record per value actually masked, structurally
971	  identical to the regular view's hit records and continuing the same
972	  per-version sequence run, plus exactly one access record whose
973	  `row_count` is the snapshot's row count and whose `masked_count` equals
974	  the number of hit records written by the read. An empty snapshot, an
975	  allowed role, all-null values and a version without policies all succeed
976	  and leave only the access record. The records enter all existing
977	  masking-hit/access reads, filters, summaries, diffs, reconciliation,
978	  trends and cleanup previews; records of one read share a write timestamp,
979	  sequences stay continuous across processes, and a write obstruction never
980	  fails the read. The read never modifies or deletes the snapshot or its
981	  rows and never changes policies or identification records. Unknown
982	  dataset/version → `404`, and no snapshot existing at or before the
983	  timestamp is likewise `404`, both checked before every shape check (the
984	  latter whenever the body carries a usable timestamp); a missing or
985	  wrong-typed `role`/`timestamp`, a role blank after trimming, an
986	  unparseable or timezone-less timestamp, an extra body field, an empty,
987	  whitespace-only or non-JSON body, a non-object body and any query
988	  parameter are `422` and write nothing.
989	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/diff/{other_snapshot_id}` —
990	  compare two snapshots as JSON-object multisets. Object key order does not
991	  affect equality, while array order and JSON value types do (e.g. `1`, `1.0`,
992	  `"1"` and `true` are all distinct), and duplicate rows are counted. Both
993	  snapshots must belong to the dataset and version named in the path, otherwise
994	  `422`; unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404`. The response is
995	  `{"from_snapshot_id", "to_snapshot_id", "added", "removed"}`; `added` lists
996	  rows present more often (or only) in the `to` snapshot and `removed` the
997	  converse, each entry being `{"row": {...}, "count": <int>}` sorted by the
998	  canonical (key-sorted) JSON text of `row`.
999	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/snapshots/{base_snapshot_id}/diff/{target_snapshot_id}` —
1000	  read-only comparison of two snapshots belonging to two **different** schema
1001	  versions of the path dataset; the baseline snapshot is named first and the
1002	  target second, and either version order is allowed. It takes no request
1003	  body and no query parameters (`422`). Unknown dataset or snapshot → `404`,
1004	  checked ahead of every request-shape check; a snapshot owned by another
1005	  dataset, or two snapshots of the same schema version (same-version
1006	  comparisons still go through the snapshot-id diff endpoint) → `422`. The
1007	  JSON document is deterministic (fixed key order, compact whitespace,
1008	  exactly one trailing newline) with top-level keys `base_snapshot_id`,
1009	  `base_version`, `target_snapshot_id`, `target_version`, `field_changes`,
1010	  `added` and `removed` in that order. `field_changes` lists only additions,
1011	  removals, type changes and nullability changes of the two versions' field
1012	  definitions, reusing the compatibility/trajectory literals (`added`,
1013	  `removed`, `type_changed`, `nullable_tightened`, `nullable_loosened`);
1014	  several changes of one field collapse into a single entry (a type change
1015	  wins over a nullability change), entries sort by field name and each entry
1016	  has `field`, `kind`, `before` and `after`, with the missing side `null`
1017	  (never omitted). Rows are projected onto exactly the field names defined
1018	  in both versions — other stored keys and fields absent from a row do not
1019	  participate — and the projections are compared with the same-version
1020	  snapshot diff's multiset semantics (object key order irrelevant, array
1021	  order and value types significant, duplicates counted). `added` lists
1022	  rows present more often or only on the target side, `removed` the
1023	  converse, each entry `{"row", "count"}` sorted by the canonical
1024	  (key-sorted) JSON text of the projected row. The comparison is fully
1025	  read-only: snapshots, rows, field definitions, the lineage impact cache
1026	  and every privacy trail are never touched, and the result is identical
1027	  across process restarts.
1028	- `POST /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/quality-rules/evaluate`
1029	  — evaluate the version's enabled quality rules over the snapshot's persisted
1030	  rows. The endpoint takes no request body and no query parameters (`422`);
1031	  unknown dataset/version/snapshot → `404` (checked first), and a snapshot
1032	  owned by another version → `422`. The response and the rule semantics are
1033	  exactly those of the row-submission evaluation (`{"dataset", "version",
1034	  "results"}`), the snapshot and its rows are never modified, and every
1035	  successful evaluation appends the same immutable history summary (with
1036	  `row_count` set to the snapshot's actual row count) that also feeds the
1037	  evaluation diff and anomaly detection. An empty snapshot is recorded with
1038	  zero violations.
1039	
1040	### Snapshot diff cache (incremental, maintained at write time)
1041	
1042	Every snapshot carries an incrementally maintained diff-cache record: when a
1043	snapshot is created, the canonical form of its rows (one key-sorted compact
1044	JSON text per row, in stored row order) and the sorted set of its top-level
1045	field names are written atomically together with the snapshot and its
1046	fingerprint. The same-version snapshot diff, the bare and masked time diffs
1047	and the two cross-version snapshot comparisons synthesize their result from

1058	- `GET /datasets/{dataset}/versions/{version}/snapshots/cache-audit` —
